title: Abnormal Psychology Adventure 1: Defining Abnormality
welcome_lead: Today you'll weigh four definitions of abnormality and meet the DSM-5.
meta_desc: IBDP Psychology Abnormal: definitions of abnormality, DSM-5 and ICD-11 classification systems.
final_note: You compared four definitions of abnormality and the main classification systems.

walkthroughs.body_html:
No single definition fits all cases.

1. Statistical infrequency — rarity. But high IQ is also rare.
2. Deviation from social norms — but norms change (homosexuality, removed from DSM 1973).
3. Failure to function adequately — Rosenhan & Seligman 1989.
4. Deviation from ideal mental health — Jahoda 1958.

DSM-5 (APA, 2013): the American Psychiatric Association manual. Categorical with some dimensional cross-cutting.

ICD-11 (WHO, 2019/2022): more globally used, includes 'complex PTSD' and 'gaming disorder'.

Both use clusters of symptoms with duration criteria.

Rosenhan (1973): 'On being sane in insane places' — 8 pseudo-patients were admitted reporting hearing 'thud'. Once labelled schizophrenic, normal behaviour was reinterpreted as symptoms.

Modern DSM-5 has better inter-rater reliability but is still critiqued for cultural bias and medicalising distress.
